concept.title: Read the caller-visible contract
paragraphs: Start with the receiver, input types, return type, and accessibility. A return type promises what a successful caller receives; it does not hide failure meaning.
Use IntelliSense one parameter or member at a time rather than memorizing a dense signature.

concept.title: Modern does not automatically mean clearer
paragraphs: Prefer the form that makes this business rule easiest to read and maintain. Older or more explicit syntax can remain the better teaching or production choice.
Compiler diagnostics identify unsupported language versions, inaccessible members, missing required values, and unsafe nullable paths.

lab.title: Records and Modern Object Construction
lab.objective: Compare explicit immutable classes with records, required/init members, primary constructors, and collection expressions without treating shorter syntax as automatically better.
lab.startingCondition: Prerequisites: the .NET SDK, VS Code or another C# editor, and basic ability to run dotnet commands. No numbered session or optional module is required. Create exercises/refreshers/r5 from scratch.

steps.text: Step 1/12: Create an isolated console project with dotnet new console -o exercises/refreshers/r5. Do not add it to PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln and do not edit TimeClock production code.
Step 2/12: Open exercises/refreshers/r5/Program.cs and remove only the template Hello World statement.
Step 3/12: At the top of Program.cs, add a comment naming the scenario: Create immutable subscription-plan summaries.
Step 4/12: Confirm the isolated project uses C# 12 or newer.
Step 5/12: Write an explicit immutable-class version in comments with a constructor and get-only properties.
Step 6/12: Create public sealed record SubscriptionPlan with primary-constructor parameter Name.
Step 7/12: Add required decimal MonthlyPrice with init; required makes construction responsibility visible but does not validate price rules.
Step 8/12: Add Features initialized with an empty collection expression.
Step 9/12: Construct one plan with an object initializer and create an annual copy with with.
Step 10/12: Run the project, compare value-oriented record syntax with the explicit class, and state when the class may be clearer.
Step 11/12: Build with dotnet build exercises/refreshers/r5 --configuration Release. Read any diagnostic before changing code.
Step 12/12: Run with dotnet run --project exercises/refreshers/r5 --configuration Release, then open Solution Reveal and compare every line.

reveals.title: Solution
reveals.text: Complete isolated solution. Keep it in this module folder only.

lab.expectedBehavior: The isolated Records and Modern Object Construction example builds and runs without referencing TimeClock or another optional module.

dotnet run --project exercises/refreshers/r5 --configuration Release
